parts:
I think you want to use subset to choose what date (lines) to display, then map specific colours to values of I. But you want to retain the scale as though the full set of values was there.

Hmmm, I'm seeing the same thing as you. At first I thought, use a subset then specify scale_colour_hue(breaks=ordered(d.p$I)) (ie say that you want the original breaks. That didn't work.

Then I thought:

dataSub <- subset(data, I > -0.5) # leave only -0.4, -0.2 and 0
dataSub$I <- ordered(dataSub$I) # make it an ordered factor
levels(dataSub$I) <- ordered(data$I) # but with all the original levels.

then

ggplot(dataSub, aes(x=K, y=err, group=I, colour=I)) + geom_line() + scale_colour_hue()

but that also didn't work, doesn't seem that ggplot respects the additional 'phantom' levels. Perhaps you'll have to map the colors and values manually using scale_colour_manual, not sure how you find out the values that scale_colour_hue picked though.

--J

messages.subject: Re: Removing entire lines from a plot without changing the colors used for the lines
parts:
All of the "sequential" and "diverging" Brewer palettes include white
as one of the gradient stops. When used for line plots, this means
several of the palette entries have insufficient contrast with
ggplot's default light grey background, which is a shame, because
otherwise I really like the Brewer color schemes.

My current kludge is

scale_colour_manual(values=colorRampPalette(c("#3B4FB8", "#B71B1A"))(6))

for the base plot, and

scale_colour_manual(values=colorRampPalette(c("#3B4FB8", "#B71B1A"))(6)[1:3])

for the one with some lines removed.

parts:
I didnt think this was going to work, but it appears to

ggplot() + 
geom_line(data=d.p[which(d.p$I==-1),],aes(x=K, y=err, group=I, colour=ordered(I))) + 
geom_line(data=d.p[which(d.p$I==-.8),],aes(x=K, y=err, group=I, colour=ordered(I))) + geom_line(data=d.p[which(d.p$I==-.6),],aes(x=K, y=err, group=I, colour=ordered(I))) + geom_line(data=d.p[which(d.p$I==-.4),],aes(x=K, y=err, group=I, colour=ordered(I))) + geom_line(data=d.p[which(d.p$I==-.2),],aes(x=K, y=err, group=I, colour=ordered(I)))+ geom_line(data=d.p[which(d.p$I==0),],aes(x=K, y=err, group=I, colour=ordered(I))) + scale_colour_hue(breaks=c(-1,-.8,-.6,-.4, -.2, 0))

I took out a single line (throw a comment in front of your choices) and it preserves the desired color scheme! Given your data frame, you probably wont mind the typing. ;) It's a cludge too, at least syntactically. The first, clean approach is desirable.

I'd already provided a second kludge, cause I do see your problem with the brewer scales you mentioned, you have a gradient so the use of qualitative scales is out. You could leave out low-contrast colours via e.g.

scale_color_manual(values = c(brewer.pal(8, 'Spectral')[c(8,7,6,3,2,1)]))

or you could rearrange qualitative palettes to give you the desired look. of course this becomes dumb for larger sets of colors or if it needs to be automated.

It'd still be nice to get color_scale_hue values to be able to set them by hand at other times.

James

I'd already provided a second kludge, cause I do see your problem with the brewer scales you mentioned, you have a gradient so the use of qualitative scales is out. You could leave out low-contrast colours via e.g.

scale_color_manual(values = c(brewer.pal(8, 'Spectral')[c(8,7,6,3,2,1)]))

or you could rearrange qualitative palettes to give you the desired look. of course this becomes dumb for larger sets of colors or if it needs to be automated.

It'd still be nice to get color_scale_hue values to be able to set them by hand at other times.

James

You could use the function in scale_hue that selects the colors. A
standalone version is in the new scales package,

https://github.com/hadley/scales/raw/master/R/pal-hue.r

(for some reason I can't source() this url so I copy it here)

hue_pal <- function(h = c(0, 360) + 15, c = 100, l = 65, h.start = 0,
direction = 1) {

function(n) {
if ((diff(h) %% 360) < 1) {
h[2] <- h[2] - 360 / n
}

rotate <- function(x) (x + h.start) %% 360 * direction
hues <- rotate(seq(h[1], h[2], length = n))

hcl(hues, c, l)
}
}

hue_pal()(5)

library(gridExtra)
grid.colorstrip(hue_pal()(5)[c(1, 3, 5)])

The limit for the discrete scale are the values you want to show. You
probably want
ggplot(d.p, aes(x=K, y=err, group=I, colour=ordered(I))) + geom_line() +

scale_colour_hue(limits = c(-1, -0.8, -0.6, -0.4, -0.2, 0))

last_plot() %+% subset(d.p, I < -0.5)
